candidates.attacker_control: The unvalidated directory-path value supplied by the application to getValidDirectoryPath / assertValidFileUpload / isValidFileUpload (typically a user-supplied upload or browse directory field). The value is attacker-controlled where the application forwards request data into these Validator APIs.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: DefaultValidator.getValidFileName appears to already contain canonical-name and canonical-path equality checks plus a FileName regex that forbids separators, ':' and '\\', so I did not find a traversal bypass in the file-name path. DefaultHTTPUtilities.getFileUploads splits the multipart name on '/' and '\\' and re-validates the last component; SafeFile explicitly documents that it does not protect against directory traversal; sendForward/getRequestDispatcher use prefix checks ('WEB-INF', allowableContentRoot) but their targets are normally application/channel-controlled rather than direct user input. No evidence was found of a missing MAC check, weak randomizer, disabled CSRF/intrusion checks, or an authorization fail-open in the reviewed code.
candidates.impact: Containment bypass/path traversal: an attacker-influenced directory value can point outside the intended parent directory while still passing ESAPI validation, so an application using assertValidFileUpload/getValidDirectoryPath can be induced to read or write files outside the intended upload/working directory (e.g., write an uploaded file into an attacker-influenced adjacent directory, or use the returned path in a subsequent filesystem operation). Impact is bounded by what the call site does with the validated path.
candidates.prerequisites: An application must (a) pass a user-controllable directory path to Validator.getValidDirectoryPath / assertValidFileUpload with a security-relevant parent (e.g., the configured upload root), and (b) use the returned/validated path for a filesystem operation. No special privileges or race conditions are required; the target directory must exist (the code requires dir.exists()/isDirectory()).
candidates.root_cause: DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath validates that the canonical directory path is inside the supplied parent with `!dir.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalPath())` (DefaultValidator.java line 469). Because no trailing File.separator (or Path.relativize/canonical-parent check) is used, any existing directory whose canonical path merely begins with the parent's path string is accepted. The subsequent canonical==input check (line 476) does not help, because an absolute attacker-chosen path is equal to its own canonical path. The documented guarantee in Validator.getValidDirectoryPath (Validator.java lines 252-271: input must map to an existing subdirectory of the specified parent) is therefore not enforced. The same helper is invoked by assertValidFileUpload/isValidFileUpload (DefaultValidator.java lines 798-824).
candidates.title: Directory containment check in DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath uses unanchored String.startsWith prefix comparison
candidates.trace: input = "/srv/uploads-evil/dir", parent = new File("/srv/uploads") -> dir.exists() and dir.isDirectory() are true, parent checks pass, dir.getCanonicalPath() = "/srv/uploads-evil/dir" startsWith "/srv/uploads" => true (line 469 check passes), fileValidator.getValidInput(canonicalPath, "DirectoryName") passes because the default DirectoryName regex allows ':' '/' '\\' and the canonical path equals input (line 476), so the path outside the intended parent is returned to the caller/assertValidFileUpload passes. The same reasoning applies to sibling directories such as "<parent>-backup" or "<parent>2".
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or upstream patch/diff comparison was possible, so I could not confirm the exact upstream fix line or the CVE mapping; exploitability depends on an application forwarding an attacker-controlled directory value into this API and on how the returned path is used. The directory must exist for the check to be reached.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Path Traversal / improper containment check (prefix comparison without separator)

coverage_summary: All 301 model-visible files were enumerated (212 Java sources plus configuration, documentation, scripts and build files). I read/traced the security-critical areas: Validator/DefaultValidator (input, file name, directory, file upload, redirect), Encoder and all codecs, crypto (JavaEncryptor, CipherText, CipherTextSerializer, KeyDerivationFunction, CryptoHelper, CryptoToken, CipherSpec), DefaultHTTPUtilities and the servlet filters/wrappers, Authenticator/FileBasedAuthenticator/User/DefaultUser, AccessController/FileBasedACRs, DefaultSecurityConfiguration defaults and ESAPI.properties, WAF filter/rules/configuration, logging appenders/scrubbers, and utility classes. Non-Java build/documentation files were scanned more selectively. Test sources are not present in the snapshot, so test-based evidence could not be used.
limitations: No upstream source, git history, patch, or CVE/CWE data was available, so I could not diff this snapshot against the fixed version or confirm which function a later security fix touched.
No code was executed and no tests were run; findings are static source analysis only and are not runtime-confirmed.
Exploitability of the reported containment bypass depends on an application passing attacker-controlled directory paths into the Validator APIs and using the result for filesystem access.

Static reading cannot fully exclude subtle bypasses in large classes (e.g., JavaEncryptor, CipherTextSerializer, DefaultSecurityConfiguration) or in dependency behavior (commons-fileupload, AntiSamy, XOM), which I did not exhaustively line-by-line audit.

rejected_leads.reason: The implementation resolves the input with getCanonicalFile().getName(), re-validates via the FileName regex (no '/' '\' ':' separators), and requires input.equals(canonical last component); percent/HTML-encoded traversal payloads are decoded and rejected by the regex. I found no bypass, so this looks like the post-fix code rather than the vulnerable version.

Non-alphanumeric characters are entity-encoded; illegal control characters are replaced with U+FFFD; named/numeric entities and non-BMP code points are encoded; JavaScript uses \xHH/\uHHHH and CSS uses hex escapes. I could not construct an XSS bypass from the code, and no concrete vulnerable line was identified.

Also prefix-based, but the forward/dispatcher target is normally supplied by application code rather than directly by an attacker; no attacker-controlled path into these was identified in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: SafeFile does not block '..' in parent path
rejected_leads.reason: This is explicitly documented in the class javadoc ('This does _not_ prevent against directory traversal attacks'), i.e., intended behavior rather than a regression, and SafeFile is not used elsewhere in the codebase.

rejected_leads.lead: Weak password hashing / 8-character CSRF token / 6-character access-reference-map tokens
rejected_leads.reason: These are documented upstream weaknesses (FileBasedAuthenticator.hashPassword javadoc; fixed token lengths) with no source-level deviation indicating an injected or fixable defect in this snapshot.
Executable must be absolute, canonical and on the configured allow-list; arguments are passed as an argv list with environment cleared, so no shell injection was evident.

summary: Reviewed the ESAPI Java 2.2.3.1 snapshot (212 main-source Java files, configuration, WAF policy/docs; no test sources included). Most security-critical code (encoder/codecs, crypto, HTTP utilities, filters, authenticator/user, access control, validator input/redirect/file-name checks, executor allow-list, WAF rules) matches the expected upstream design and fails closed in the places I could verify. The strongest source-supported issue is a broken containment check in DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath(): the "inside parent" test is a raw String.startsWith prefix comparison with no path-separator boundary, so a canonical path that merely shares the parent's string prefix is accepted even though it is not a subdirectory of the parent. This violates the explicit contract in the Validator interface ("an existing subdirectory (at any level) of the specified parent") and is reachable from the file-upload validation API (assertValidFileUpload / isValidFileUpload), i.e., a path-traversal/containment bypass lead.
